description: Stage 3c gate: the show thread must keep advancing while the editor thread is stalled. Loads the gradient PNG sequence, starts playback, then blocks the editor thread for 500 ms via StallEditor (simulating a Win32 modal loop). MarkShowFrameCount immediately before the stall and AssertShowFrameCountAdvancedBy in the first drain after it measure exactly the stall window: a re-introduced condvar gate (Stage 3b) or a deadlocked show thread yields ~0 frames in that window, while even a slow WARP CI runner (~10 Hz show ticks) yields ~5. The old cumulative AssertShowFrameCountAtLeast 20 mixed pre-stall frames into the count and assumed 60 Hz pacing — and, worse, a wait-based form would count post-stall recovery frames, missing exactly the blocks-only-while-editor-is-blocked regression this test exists to catch. (Was SleepMs until issue #74 — SleepMs no longer blocks the editor thread, which had quietly weakened this test.)
